plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, paying that amount, and never overpay. Bidding above value risks winning at a price exceeding my value; bidding below value risks losing profitable wins. With value $24, the optimal bid is simply $24, regardless of opponents' bidding behavior.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding higher than your value risks paying more than the item is worth, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $16, I should bid exactly $16 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I win whenever it's profitable and pay only the second-highest bid when I do win.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning and paying more than the item is worth; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $24.
